info.desc: Elastica is the debut studio album by English alternative rock band Elastica. It was released on 13 March 1995 through Deceptive Records in the UK and DCG/Geffen Records internationally. The album was nominated for the Mercury Music Prize. This is the only album to feature the original line-up, and guitarist Donna Matthews. .

podcast.body: Elastica's debut album, released in March 1995, was characterized as fresh, fun, good, and familiar-sounding. It contributed significantly to the Britpop movement, with a single from the album having been released in November 1994. "Elastica's debut album was also fresh, very fun, and very good, and also familiar soundings."

podcast.body: Released in March 1995, this album became the fastest-selling debut album in UK history, achieving worldwide sales of over a million copies and earning numerous awards, including a Mercury Prize nomination. It spawned five hit singles. "When Elastica's debut album was released in March 1995, it became the fastest-selling debut album in the history of the UK."

podcast.body: The band's first album contained songs like "Connection" and "Waking Up," both of which led to legal disputes due to their similarities with tracks by other artists. As a result of these cases, Elastica was ordered to surrender a portion of the royalties from this album to both Wire and The Stranglers. "Elastica had to surrender a certain amount of the royalties from that first album to Wire in exchange for... paying too much homage to them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This debut album, released during the Britpop era, faced multiple claims of musical similarities. The song "Connection" was admitted by Justine Frischmann to have "nicked some of Three Girl Rumba" from Wire, leading to a surrender of a "certain amount of the royalties from that first album to Wire." Additionally, "Waking Up" was found to be similar to The Stranglers' "No More Heroes," resulting in "a piece of that first Elastica album" being awarded to The Stranglers. "The ruling was that Elastica had to surrender a certain amount of the royalties from that first album to Wire, which, you know, given her admission of guilt seems kind of fair."
